blocks.title: Key Takeaways
items: Pressure is thrust acting per unit area; smaller surface area produces higher pressure for the same force.
Pressure in liquids depends on depth, density of liquid, and acceleration due to gravity (P = hρg).
Atmospheric pressure decreases with altitude, which lowers the boiling point of liquids.
Archimedes' Principle states that the buoyant force equals the weight of the fluid displaced by an immersed body.
Relative density has no units as it is the ratio of a substance's density to water's density at 4°C.

blocks.content: Pressure is defined as the force acting per unit area.
It tells us how much force is applied on a particular area. Formula:
SI Unit of Pressure = Pascal (Pa) 1 Pascal = 1 Newton / m²

items: A sharp knife cuts easily because it has small area → more pressure.
A camel walks easily on sand because it has broad feet → less pressure.
High-heeled shoes exert more pressure than flat shoes.

• Force applied
  • Area of contact
Force applied
Area of contact

blocks.content: If area is less → pressure is more If area is more → pressure is less
Liquids also exert pressure. Important points:

items:
• Liquid pressure increases with depth
  • Liquid pressure acts in all directions
  • Liquid pressure depends on height of liquid column
Liquid pressure increases with depth
Liquid pressure acts in all directions
Liquid pressure depends on height of liquid column

blocks.content: When a body is partially or fully immersed in a fluid, it experiences an upward force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced by it.
The pressure exerted by air on the surface of the Earth is called atmospheric pressure. We do not feel atmospheric pressure because it acts equally in all directions.

blocks.content: The upward force exerted by a liquid on an object immersed in it is called buoyant force. This force helps objects to float.

blocks.content: When a body is immersed partially or completely in a fluid, it experiences an upward force equal to the weight of the fluid displaced.

blocks.content: An object floats or sinks depending upon its density.
If density of object < density of liquid → object floats If density of object > density of liquid → object sinks
Density is defined as mass per unit volume. Formula:
Density = Mass / Volume SI unit = kg/m³
Objects with higher density sink in water.

Sudden drop in barometer reading indicates a storm, while a slow fall predicts rain.
Lactometer (milk purity) and Hydrometer (liquid density) are based on Archimedes' Principle.
Hydraulic brakes, lifts, and presses work on Pascal's Law.
Dams are made thicker at the bottom because liquid pressure increases with depth.
